approach.method_basis: The Parent is a genetic algorithm that edits molecular graphs directly and puts a Bayesian screening step in front of the scoring oracle. It keeps every molecule scored so far in the current task, keeps the best sixty-four as its breeding population and draws parents from high score quantiles. Each candidate is made either by joining connected fragments of two scored parents, sometimes finished with one more edit, or by a short random walk of atom, bond and ring edits on one parent; that walk asks for one, two or three edits with probabilities 0.82, 0.15 and 0.03 and stops at the first edit that fails. Candidates must pass canonical-identity and duplicate checks and a narrow rule that refuses sulfur environments their scored parents did not already carry, and direct aromatic carbon-nitrogen swaps are switched off. For each batch of ten evaluations it breeds 160 fresh candidates, fits a Gaussian process with a Tanimoto-style kernel over integer Morgan substructure counts to this task's scores alone, draws ten correlated posterior samples over the 160 candidates and evaluates their maxima one at a time. All of these settings are the same whether or not the search is still improving, although about a fifth of its batches come after three or more batches without a new best score and they yield only about eight percent of its realized gain.
approach.novelty: This Child changes two things about how the Parent behaves during a measured stall and ties both to one switch. It counts consecutive batches that fail to raise the session's best score; while that count stands at three or more, the next batch breeds 640 fresh candidates instead of 160 and, in the same batch, the single-parent edit walk asks for longer walks (one, two or three edits with probabilities 0.50, 0.35 and 0.15). Both return to the Parent's settings on the first batch that improves, and until a session first stalls the run is identical to the Parent's, random numbers included. Each half was tried alone on this Parent in the previous round and each cleared the bar on a thin margin, but each left the other half untouched: with only 160 candidates to choose from, the selector picked longer-walk candidates at about a third of the rate of ordinary ones, and the wider field was filled with ordinary short-walk candidates. Here the selector sees about four times as many longer-walk candidates in exactly the batches where it has stopped finding improvements. No value is new - the threshold, the field width and the walk law are the ones already measured - so the result answers only whether the two stall remedies compound, as a total effect of the pair. That separates it from this round's other positions on the same switch: two make the selector more conservative during stalls (less sampling noise, or choosing only among the candidates with the best predicted score), and one changes no rule at all and only perturbs the random path, supplying the reference against which this combined result is read.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-1744a1494180 (complete macro mean 0.596453, population SD 0.033970, seed macros 0.643098, 0.563173 and 0.583088) does not convert its stalled evaluation budget into realized incumbent gain. Recomputed for this plan from its fifteen published trajectories, the counter of consecutive announced batches that fail to raise the session best-so-far reaches three in 13 of 15 sessions: 29 episodes and 91 of 435 announced batches (20.9 percent) carry only 0.476561 of its 5.819415 sequential incumbent gain (8.2 percent), and deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 never stall. Round 38 tested four single changes gated by exactly this counter. Two cleared +0.002 alone, each on a thin margin: the heavier floor-one ordinary walk law (n-e5dba2059cfe, +0.007648; +0.008824 on the thirteen cells a K=3 gate can change; +0.002317 without its best cell, sitagliptin_mpo seed 1) and the fourfold fresh pool (n-25b9a57765d8, +0.004664; +0.005381; +0.001530 without its best two cells), while widened residual sampling (n-189cd716f027, -0.009718) and stall-only crossover removal (n-9e5f01d67b9f, -0.014192) lost. Each positive element changes only one side of the stalled generate-then-select step, and each single arm's own receipts show the side it leaves unchanged limiting it. Under the heavier law alone the 160-member field let the unchanged allocator emit lengthened products at about a third of the single-call rate (25.7 percent of the stalled pool against 13.9 percent of emissions; 3.37 against 10.4 percent selected per pooled final), so lengthened products directly delivered only 0.052353 of the 0.599867 in-regime sequential increment. Under the fourfold pool alone the 480 extra members competed at the exchangeable rate (0.729 of widened-batch picks at pool index 160 or higher) and stalls broke sooner (2.41 against 3.20 batches from trigger to the next improving batch), but every extra ordinary-route candidate was bred under the inherited short walk law (optional-call share about 0.18), so the wider field sampled the same mostly one-edit mutation neighbourhood more densely, and the mean accepted in-regime offspring score fell (0.3875 against 0.4046). Curate records the composition of the two channels as untested (h-435e40e1ac2f5c98), the schedule, width optimum and monotonicity as unidentified (h-0058b24c0145fb5d, h-065213eaad9d442d), and no measured reference separating a gated channel effect from gated path divergence (h-899be9ec4538ec8c). The single limiting behaviour this position responds to is that inside the stalled regime the Parent offers its allocator neither a wider fresh field nor structurally farther candidates, and neither single remedy supplies both at once.

literature_review.conclusion: A fresh search found theory-side precedent for both halves and for coupling them: the self-adjusting (1+(λ,λ)) GA raises offspring number and mutation strength together after an unsuccessful iteration, adaptive offspring-population schemes double the offspring count after failure and reset on success, and stagnation detection raises mutation strength after a no-improvement threshold. TuRBO, read directly because the frozen search-policy review names it, uses the same batch success definition but narrows after failure. None supplies a value, threshold or molecular setting and none is integrated as code, so this review is internal-evidence based with no adoptions, no asset and no dependency; the literature informs only the stated path of effect and the reading of this position beside the round's narrowing positions.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The joint intervention is fixed by campaign receipts, not by a source: both elements, their values (K=3, 64 against 16 candidates per announced member, [0.50, 0.35, 0.15] against [0.82, 0.15, 0.03]) and the shared counter were bound, verified to activate exactly and measured on this Parent in round 38 (n-e5dba2059cfe +0.007648, n-25b9a57765d8 +0.004664); the stalled regime is located by the Anchor's own fifteen trajectories (29 episodes, 91 of 435 batches, 0.476561 of 5.819415 realized sequential gain); and Curate records their composition as the open question (h-435e40e1ac2f5c98). The searched sources give precedent for coupling failure-driven increases in offspring number and step size and a contrasting narrowing response, but none supplies a value, threshold, schedule or molecular-graph setting this node uses, so no element is adopted.

sources.applicability: Closest published precedent for raising offspring number and step size together on a failure signal and lowering them on success, with selection among many offspring absorbing larger steps. It frames the stated path of effect (a wider field is what can let more lengthened products survive selection) but supplies no element, value, schedule or threshold used here: this node's switch is binary, its values are the round-38 bound values, and the paper's setting is a pseudo-Boolean benchmark, not a 300-evaluation molecular search with a learned selector. Nothing is adopted.
sources.finding: In the (1+(λ,λ)) GA one parameter λ sets both the number of offspring and the mutation strength: one strength ℓ ~ Bin(n, λ/n) is drawn per iteration and λ mutation offspring each flip ℓ bits, followed by λ crossover offspring with bias 1/λ; after an iteration without improvement λ is multiplied by F^(1/4), after a success it is divided by F, which yields linear expected optimization time on OneMax.
sources.title: Optimal Parameter Choices Through Self-Adjustment: Applying the 1/5-th Rule in Discrete Settings (Benjamin Doerr and Carola Doerr, arXiv 1504.03212) - full text

sources.applicability: Precedent for widening the offspring field after failure and resetting it on success, which is the shape of the fresh-pool element here (one fixed fourfold step, restored on the first improving batch, rather than repeated doubling). That element was already bound and measured on this Parent; no value or schedule is borrowed.
sources.finding: Both proposed schemes double the number of offspring instances when a generation ends without an improvement; on success the first scheme resets to one instance and the second halves it. Both give near-optimal parallel-time speed-ups with sequential evaluation bounds no larger than those of the corresponding non-parallel algorithm (abstract-level reading).
sources.title: Adaptive Population Models for Offspring Populations and Parallel Evolutionary Algorithms (Jörg Lässig and Dirk Sudholt, arXiv 1102.0588)

sources.applicability: Precedent for the longer-walk element: a strength increase triggered by a no-improvement counter and reset on improvement. It does not couple the increase with more offspring, so it neither supports nor rules out compounding, and its threshold formula assumes a known neighbourhood size that this molecular walk does not have. Nothing is adopted.
sources.finding: Stagnation detection counts iterations without strict improvement and raises the mutation strength once the count exceeds a threshold, resetting strength and counter on a strict improvement; in the (1+λ) version the threshold is divided by λ and, in stagnation mode, all λ offspring use the same increasing strength while λ itself is unchanged.
sources.title: Self-Adjusting Evolutionary Algorithms for Multimodal Optimization (Amirhossein Rajabi and Carsten Witt, arXiv 2004.03266) - full text

sources.applicability: Same batch-level success definition as the shared counter here, but the opposite response to failure: TuRBO narrows sampling after repeated failures, whereas this composition broadens generation (more candidates and longer walks). This round's positions 1 and 4 test the narrowing response on the same trigger, so the two directions are read side by side and descriptively. Nothing is adopted here.
sources.finding: A batch is a success if at least one of its evaluations improves the best solution; after tau_succ = 3 consecutive successes the trust region doubles and after tau_fail = ceil(d/q) consecutive failures it halves, the counters reset when the region changes, and Thompson sampling selects from min{100d, 5000} fresh candidates per batch.
sources.title: Scalable Global Optimization via Local Bayesian Optimization (TuRBO; Eriksson, Pearce, Gardner, Turner and Poloczek, arXiv 1910.01739) - full text

hypothesis: Couple the two measured stall-gated elements to one shared trigger on the Parent. One integer counter of consecutive non-improving announced batches, computed only from this session's accepted scores exactly as in the published fresh-pool implementation (an announced batch is improving when the greedy-retained incumbent after its observations exceeds the incumbent held when the batch was announced; the counter resets to zero on any improving batch), is read once per announced batch into a single regime flag. While that flag is set (counter at or above K=3) the same announced batch both (a) breeds a fresh offspring pool of 64 candidates per announced member, 640 at batch ten, instead of 16 (160), and (b) draws the floor-one ordinary single-parent requested mutation-call length from [0.50, 0.35, 0.15] on lengths [1, 2, 3] instead of [0.82, 0.15, 0.03], with exactly one active rng.choices draw at its inherited stream position and the ORIGINAL [0.82, 0.15, 0.03] base draw with max(base, min(6, 1 + member_attempts // 80)) whenever the saturation floor exceeds one. Both revert together on the first improving batch, and nothing differs from the Parent, including random-number consumption, before a session's counter first reaches three. Path of effect: every floor-one ordinary-route candidate of a stalled 640-member pool is bred under the heavier law, so the stalled field holds about four times as many lengthened, structurally farther products as the continuation arm's 160-member field, and the unchanged accepted-only count-GP correlated Thompson allocator takes its ten sequentially masked joint-draw maxima over that larger mixed field. The causal claim is that the wider field is what can let more lengthened products survive selection, while the heavier law is what lets the extra breadth reach beyond the inherited mostly one-edit neighbourhood; if both act, stalled batches emit lengthened products drawn from beyond the inherited first 160 pool positions - a joint event that is structurally impossible in either single arm - and stalled episodes deliver larger realized incumbent increments than the Anchor's matched episodes. Allocator, GP, kernel, normalization, noise, jitter, operators and their probabilities, crossover and its finishing, sulfur gate, identity admission, parent sampling and survivors are unchanged, and no value of either element is altered.

finding_summary.headline: Both stall remedies co-acted exactly as bound and 136 joint candidates were selected, yet the panel fell 0.0051: the two do not compound
finding_summary.insights: The composition question Curate had left open is now answered, and answered negatively: the two stall remedies do not compound on this Anchor. More than that, the result closes the specific explanation each single arm's receipts had suggested for its own thin margin. The continuation arm's story was that only 160 candidates meant the selector rarely saw a lengthened product; the fresh-pool arm's story was that its 480 extra candidates were all short-walk clones of the same neighbourhood. Supplying both at once removed both limitations - the selector was offered about four times as many lengthened, structurally farther candidates in exactly the batches where the search had stopped improving, and it did pick them, 136 times from beyond the inherited pool positions - and the panel still lost. Candidate supply inside stalled batches is therefore not what was holding those two arms back, and widening generation further in this regime has no remaining rationale. What the regime did buy was breadth without quality. Stalls broke about 20 percent faster and parent-relative gain mass rose by a quarter, yet the molecules actually accepted during stalls were materially worse (0.353 against 0.405), the whole-run incumbent gain fell slightly, and the chemistry review finds the same shape: in the matched post-divergence windows this node covered slightly more scaffolds (1,006 against 968) while adding no new compound class, produced more molecules with unresolved stereocentres (1,407 against 1,206) and wasted more oracle calls on sub-seven-atom fragments (88 against 57). Deeper edits on a wider field move the search further, not upward, and in a 300-call budget the extra motion is paid for in evaluations. This sharpens a lesson the round already half-learned: stall-time arms should be judged on realized gain per exposed batch and on the quality of what is accepted, not on exposure totals, event counts or exit speed, all of which improved here while the endpoint fell. The two round-38 positives now look weaker as channel effects than they did. Their joint recipe, built from their own bound values under their own trigger, lands three times further from zero than this round's law-free reference arm - which moved -0.001735 while swinging single cells from -0.034 to +0.041 - and their largest cells and this node's largest cells sit in the same high-variance sitagliptin sessions (+0.0626 on seed 1, -0.0578 on seed 0 here). Nothing in these fifteen cells identifies which part of either margin was real. The honest next step for that question is independent-seed re-measurement of a single arm, not another gated variant of the same family; the stall-gated generate-side family itself has now produced four single arms and one composition on this Anchor without a reproducible endpoint gain, which is a reason to stop widening generation and look elsewhere for the limiting behaviour.
finding_summary.results: Activation was exact on every pre-registered count. Across the 435 announced batches of the fifteen matched sessions, the shared counter agreed with an independent recount from the Child's own accepted scores in every batch, and the 95 batches announced with the counter at three or above all bred 640 of 640 candidates untruncated under the heavier walk law, while the other 340 bred 160 of 160 under the inherited law. There was not one batch in which one element switched without the other. Inside stalled batches the floor-one walk asked for more edits on exactly the same random draws - optional-call share 0.495 against a same-draw replay of 0.181, requested mean 1.646 against 1.212 - and outside them every one of 34,345 attempts matched its replay exactly. Every extra requested edit was executed: not one of 72,113 ordinary attempts hit a failed edit. The joint event the composition existed to produce did happen: stalled pools held about 169 lengthened candidates each instead of about 41, three quarters of stalled picks came from beyond the inherited first 160 pool positions, and 136 emitted molecules were lengthened products drawn from beyond position 159 - about 1.4 per stalled batch, where either element alone makes that event impossible. Every session was identical to the Parent until its own first stalled batch, and the two sessions that never stall reproduced the Parent record for record. Cost stayed affordable: about 715 breeding attempts per stalled batch against 174, 48 seconds of mean non-oracle work per task against 26, no truncated pool, no fallback, no retry escalation, and node runtimes of 4 to 6 minutes against a 11-hour limit; the only quantity above forecast was diagnostic log volume, 168 MB for the most exposed task. The endpoint went the other way. The complete fifteen-cell matched panel fell 0.005132 (0.591322 against the Parent's 0.596453), with seed deltas -0.020329, +0.005986 and -0.001052: nine cells down, three up, three exactly equal. It is not a one-cell artefact - the thirteen cells a K=3 gate can change give -0.005921, and every leave-one-cell variant stays negative, from -0.009973 to -0.001371 - and it is far below both single arms (+0.007648 and +0.004664) and below the +0.002 bar, so the registered score-layer falsifier triggered and no sweep follows. Inside the stalled regime the realized-gain picture is marginal rather than negative: total in-regime incumbent gain 0.479568 against the Anchor's 0.476561 and gain mass 2.0688 against 1.6436, with stalls breaking in 2.5 batches instead of 3.2, but the gain per exposed batch was slightly lower (0.005048 against 0.005237), both single arms converted their stalled batches better (0.5999 and 0.6800), and the mean score of molecules accepted during stalls dropped from 0.405 to 0.353. The one comparison taken from an identical state - each session's first stalled batch, thirteen of them - is the composition's best result: 0.294 of incumbent gain against the Anchor's 0.166, the continuation arm's 0.126 and the fresh-pool arm's 0.268.

molecular.headline: Halogen-dense flat heteroaromatics plus one aminal cyclic-diamine family; leading sets carry reactive heteroatom bonds and no specified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-36afb69ebdd1 proposed 870 optimizer molecules per objective, 4350 over the five objectives and three Search seeds, from the same ten starting molecules in every session. All 15 Child staging trajectories and all 15 published Parent trajectories were present and read in full at 900 records each, and context.comparison reports child_complete true and paired_complete true on matched seeds 0, 1 and 2 with no profile-mismatched seed, so no path and no paired comparison is missing. Ring, group and size readings here come from a read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 pass over those same files; digest counters quoted as such are string-level readings of the SMILES text. The output is ring- and aromatic-rich, consistent with those counters: median 3 to 4 perceived rings and 2 to 4 perceived aromatic rings, digest ring_closure_rate 0.9598 to 0.9770 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9471 to 0.9701, median size 25 to 31 heavy atoms and mean SMILES length 43.4 to 58.5. The chemistry is flat, neutral and halogen-heavy. Not one of the 4350 molecules carries a formal charge, none carries stereochemistry notation (digest stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five objectives) while RDKit perceives at least one unassigned tetrahedral centre in 2656 of them, and 706 place a halogen on nitrogen, 384 on oxygen and 34 on sulfur. Four families recur: compact indole and azaindole 2-carboxamides of about 25 heavy atoms; nitrogen-rich fused carbonyl/thione cores linked to an azaaromatic ring; aryl-substituted six- and seven-membered cyclic diamines whose ring carbon sits between both nitrogens; and fluorinated xanthine-like fused systems. Half the panel, 2170 of 4350, carries at least one of N-halogen, O-halogen, S-halogen, peroxide, nitroso, cumulated diene, halomethyl ether, anhydride-like or three/four-membered ring motif, and among the 50 highest-scoring molecules that rate is 43/50, 50/50 and 50/50 on three objectives against 17/50 and 3/50 on the other two. Ordinary medicinal-chemistry vocabulary is largely absent: across all 4350 molecules there are 0 carbon-bound trifluoromethyl groups, 0 morpholines, 0 tetrazoles, 0 nitro groups, 1 sulfone, 3 piperazines, 25 piperidines, 109 pyrrolidines, 56 carboxylic acids and 76 sulfonamides, 75 of the sulfonamides on one objective and all of those inside its first 47 evaluations. Of the 986 molecules carrying a three- or four-membered ring, 896 have that ring unsaturated or aromatic-labelled rather than an ordinary saturated cyclopropane, azetidine or oxetane, and 69 molecules put a cumulated carbon double-bond centre inside a ring against 6 in the Parent files. Two sessions, deco_hop seeds 0 and 2, are byte-identical to the Parent record for record; the other 13 diverge from evaluation 41 to 231 onward. In those 13 matched post-divergence windows, 2339 molecules on each side, the Child occupies 1006 distinct Murcko scaffolds against the Parent's 968, and 858 of its 993 scaffolds never appear in the matched Parent session, yet its class-level group census stays within about three percentage points of the Parent on every group measured, while proposals of six heavy atoms or fewer rise to 88 from 57, molecules with a three/four-membered ring to 571 from 488, molecules with a heteroatom-halogen bond to 773 from 718, molecules with an unassigned tetrahedral centre to 1407 from 1206 and the session-average synthetic-accessibility score to 4.32 from 4.11. The extra structural reach therefore produced new arrangements of the same chemical vocabulary, with more fragmentation and more strained local geometry rather than new group classes. Everything above is an output description: no score, ranking, selection, activation or causal claim is made here.

per_task.generated_character: Compact flat tricyclics, the most recognizable set of the five: median 25 heavy atoms, 3 perceived rings, 3 aromatic rings, median MW 358, median cLogP 3.9, median QED 0.64, median SA score 3.31. The dominant family is an indole or azaindole bearing a 2-carboxanilide with methyl, ethyl and methoxy decoration - amide in 718 of 870 proposals, aromatic ring nitrogen in 719, a benzene ring in 808, aryl methyl ether in 446, basic sp3 nitrogen in 214. There are 302 distinct Murcko scaffolds over 870 proposals, but the most common one, O=C(Nc1ccccc1)c1cc2ccccc2[nH]1, covers 133 of them and is exactly the scaffold of the supplied starting molecule COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC. Halogens are heavy (digest halogen_rate 0.8713) and 335 molecules put one on a heteroatom: 323 on nitrogen, 13 on oxygen, 5 on sulfur. 34 proposals have six or fewer heavy atoms, 19 of them after evaluation 100, down to single atoms. Digest span 0.0 to 0.4394 with median 0.3155.
liabilities: N-fluoro, N-chloro or N-bromo bonds on both the amide and the ring nitrogen in all 12 digest leaders, for example CNc1c(C)c(C)cc2c1cc(C(=O)N(F)c1ccccc1)n2F at 0.4394; these are oxidants, not stable amides
323 of 870 proposals carry a direct N-halogen bond, 13 an O-halogen bond and 7 a peroxide, including OOCl at 0.0, a chlorinated peroxide

47 molecules place a cumulated carbon double-bond centre inside a ring against 0 in the matched Parent files; one endpoint, CNC=C(C)C1=CC=C(C(=O)Nc2cccc(Br)c2)SC=C=C(Br)O1 at 0.3900, puts it in a nine-membered ring, and digest cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.0563 is the highest of the five objectives
N-O single bonds in 96 proposals, including the halogen-free endpoint Cc1c2c(cc3c1SC=C(C(=O)Nc1ccccc1)N3)ON(C)C2 at 0.4216 whose fused N-O closure needs separate assessment
34 degenerate proposals of six heavy atoms or fewer, among them a bare Br atom at 0.0, each consuming one of 300 oracle calls
missing_features: no carbon-bound trifluoromethyl or difluoromethyl group in the 870 proposals, despite digest halogen_rate 0.8713, so halogen demand is met at ring and amide nitrogens instead
aromatic nitrile is effectively absent (1 of 870) although a nitrile-bearing molecule sits in the supplied starting set
saturated nitrogen heterocycles that add polarity without a reactive bond are nearly unrepresented: 11 pyrrolidines, 0 piperidines, 0 piperazines and 0 morpholines in 870 proposals
fused diazine cores are rare (8 pyrimidine-containing proposals of 870), so the bicyclic core is explored almost only by peripheral substitution
no ordinary N-alkyl tertiary amide among the leaders; every one of the 12 digest leaders reaches a substituted amide nitrogen through a halogen rather than a carbon group
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Size and completeness of the three-ring aromatic amide dominate: mean score 0.3152 for 23-27 heavy atoms against 0.1400 for 15-22 and 0.1572 for 28-33, and the two proposals above 33 atoms score 0.0. Amide-bearing molecules average 0.3082 against 0.2639 without one, aromatic-ring-nitrogen 0.3074 against 0.2695, benzene 0.3038 against 0.2503. N-halogenated molecules average 0.3312 against 0.2843 and all 12 digest leaders carry a direct N-halogen bond, but matched pairs in this node's own files show no consistent reward: 23 pairs differing only by one halogen on a heteroatom average +0.0078 with 11 favouring the halogenated form. COc1c(C)c(C)cc2[nH]c(C(=O)N(F)c3ccccc3)cc12 at 0.4272 beats its plain amide COc1c(C)c(C)cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccccc3)cc12 at 0.3783, while inside the leading family the plain secondary amide CCc1c(OC)cc2c(c1C)c(Cl)c(C(=O)Nc1ccccn1)n2F at 0.4388 beats its N-fluoro analogue CCc1c(OC)cc2c(c1C)c(Cl)c(C(=O)N(F)c1ccccn1)n2F at 0.4241. Six digest leaders sit at an identical 0.4388 and differ only in which halogen occupies two positions, so the top of this objective is a halogen-permutation plateau rather than a gradient the molecules are still climbing.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: Fluorine count is the clearest monotone association on the panel: among proposals above 15 heavy atoms the mean score rises 0.0485, 0.1246, 0.2309, 0.3204, 0.3223 for zero, one, two, three and four or more fluorines. Basic sp3 nitrogen averages 0.2959 against 0.1955, aryl methyl ether 0.2967 against 0.1935, a three/four-membered ring 0.2706 against 0.1791, while the 21 amide-bearing molecules sit at 0.0306 and the 23-27 atom band peaks at 0.2402. The generator satisfies the fluorine association by putting F wherever a valence is free, nitrogen included: the leader COc1ccc(F)cc1-n1cc2c(c1C1(C)C=CN1)c(=O)n(F)c(=N)n2F at 0.6365 carries two N-F bonds and one aryl F. Where the extra halogen lands on a heteroatom in an otherwise identical pair the label collapses - all 11 matched pairs favour the dehalogenated form at mean -0.1647, and COc1cc(S)ccc1-n1cc2c(c1C1(F)C=CCN1)c(=O)n(F)c(=NCl)n2F scores 0.0760 against 0.6328 for COc1cc(S)ccc1-n1cc2c(c1C1(F)C=CCN1)c(=O)n(F)c(=N)n2F. The association is fluorine density on a compact nitrogen-rich core with a free imine or amine; the liabilities ride along rather than being rewarded.

transferable_gaps.evidence: None of the ten supplied starting molecules any session begins from carries a halogen on a heteroatom, yet across the 4350 optimizer proposals 706 molecules place a halogen on nitrogen, 384 on oxygen and 34 on sulfur. On two objectives the single highest-scoring molecule carries two direct N-F bonds, and on a third all three joint-best molecules carry an aryl O-F bond. The search is not following a consistent signal there: of 51 matched pairs in this node's own trajectories that differ only by one halogen on a heteroatom, the halogenated form is higher in only 15, and the per-objective mean differences are +0.0078, -0.0033, -0.0090, -0.1298 and -0.1647. In one case the plain secondary amide CCc1c(OC)cc2c(c1C)c(Cl)c(C(=O)Nc1ccccn1)n2F scores 0.4388 against 0.4241 for its N-fluoro analogue, and in another the free N-H amine CCCc1cc(Br)cc(CN2CCCCNC2c2cccc(Cl)c2)c1 scores 0.9798 against 0.7725 for its N-fluoro form, so the motif is a local plateau the proposal stream keeps re-entering rather than a route the labels demand.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator attaches halogens to nitrogen, oxygen and sulfur as freely as to carbon, and treats that as one more atom swap.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Atom-identity and substituent operators should treat halogen attachment to N, O or S as a distinct edit class, gated or filtered at pool admission the way the existing sulfur-environment rule already filters one motif class, and should offer a carbon-attachment alternative for the same requested edit. The aim is not to forbid the motif but to stop whole leading series being reachable only through it, and to stop a surrogate fitted on accepted observations learning that halogen-on-heteroatom is the cheapest available substituent. No causal score benefit from such a filter is established by this output evidence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In 4350 optimizer proposals there are zero carbon-bound trifluoromethyl groups and only 13 carbon-bound difluoromethyl groups, while 1764 molecules carry an aryl fluorine and the digest halogen_rate reaches 0.8713, 0.8851 and 0.9759 on three objectives. On one objective the mean score rises monotonically with fluorine count, 0.0485, 0.1246, 0.2309, 0.3204 and 0.3223 for zero through four or more fluorines, and the generator answers that signal by placing fluorine on ring nitrogens (297 of 870 molecules) and on oxygen (196 of 870) instead. The Parent trajectories show the same zero count, so this is a standing property of the operator set rather than something this intervention changed.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot build a carbon-bound polyfluoroalkyl group, the ordinary way to raise halogen content without adding a labile bond.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The atom and bond operators need a route from a methyl or aryl-H position to a fully halogenated carbon substituent in one accepted edit, rather than only single halogen additions that the walk then places wherever a free valence exists. A multi-halogen carbon substituent is a single chemical unit in practice and the proposal stream currently has no way to request it, which is why halogen demand is met at heteroatoms.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The ten starting molecules contain only five- and six-membered rings, so every small and medium ring in the output was built by the generator. Of the 986 proposals carrying a three- or four-membered ring, 896 have it unsaturated or aromatic-labelled and only 90 carry an ordinary saturated three- or four-membered ring; in all 4350 proposals there are just 18 saturated azetidines and 18 saturated cyclopropanes. Leading molecules inherit these closures: one family's best molecule fuses three four-membered rings to a benzene, another's has a three-membered ring that RDKit perceives as aromatic, 13 proposals put a triple bond inside a ring and 69 put a cumulated carbon double-bond centre inside a ring against 6 such molecules in the Parent files, one of them in a nine-membered ring at a session endpoint. In the 13 matched post-divergence windows the count of molecules with a three/four-membered ring rises to 571 from the baseline's 488 over the same 2339 proposals, so deeper edit walks add more of these closures rather than fewer.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-forming edits produce strained and unsaturated small rings rather than ordinary saturated ones, and nothing distinguishes valence-valid closures from geometrically credible ones.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction, ring-bond and bond-order operators need sensitivity to ring size, ring unsaturation and bridge connectivity, and should be able to offer a saturated or larger-ring alternative that keeps the same connectivity the feedback favoured. Ring richness itself is not the problem and a blanket ban on small, fused or medium rings is not what this evidence supports; the missing capability is choosing among credible closures.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on all five objectives, and no proposal in the 4350 carries stereochemistry notation, while RDKit perceives at least one unassigned tetrahedral centre in 2656 of them. The concentration is worst exactly where the output is most ligand-like: 837 of 870 proposals on one objective and 1 to 4 unassigned centres in each of its 12 highest-scoring molecules, including a saturated diamine ring whose configuration decides the whole shape. In the 13 matched post-divergence windows the count rises to 1407 from 1206, so the deeper edit regime created more unresolved centres. Some leaders have no tetrahedral centre at all, so this applies where a generated structure needs a configuration, not to every molecule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic centres are left unspecified in every molecule the generator emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Operators that create or destroy a tetrahedral centre should resolve or preserve its configuration, and the identity and duplicate checks should distinguish configurations that are chemically distinct. Treat achiral and configurationally unstable cases as such, and assess protonation and tautomer notation separately; nothing here shows the labels penalise an unspecified centre, only that the generator never states one.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across all 4350 optimizer proposals there are zero formal charges, 56 carboxylic acids, 76 sulfonamides, 1 sulfone and 0 tetrazoles. The supplied starting population already contains a sulfonamide and a carboxylic acid, and every single proposal carrying either group appears by evaluation 62 of 300 - the last sulfonyl-bearing proposal anywhere in the panel is evaluation 47 - after which neither group is ever rebuilt in any of the 15 sessions. Basic centres, by contrast, are common: 1599 molecules carry a basic sp3 nitrogen and on one objective such molecules average 0.6842 against 0.1069 without one, yet every one of them is written neutral, so the output never represents the charge state in which that centre acts.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits no ionizable or formally charged species and essentially never constructs an acidic group.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operator set needs a route to build ionizable groups, acidic as well as basic, rather than only inheriting them from the starting population, and the representation should be able to carry a protonation state when it is chemically meaningful. The absence is a capability gap in the proposal stream, not a demonstrated score penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 144 of the 4350 optimizer proposals have six or fewer heavy atoms and 95 of those arrive after the hundredth evaluation, when the population already holds molecules near the session best; they include single atoms, C=C, C#C, FF, OOCl and a six-carbon chain emitted as evaluation 297 of 300. Each consumes one oracle call from a budget of 300 and sits at or near the objective floor. The matched baseline emits 113 such proposals, and inside the 13 matched post-divergence windows the Child's count is 88 against 57 over the same 2339 proposals, while its session-average synthetic-accessibility score rose to 4.32 from 4.11, so in this node's own matched windows the degenerate-proposal count is about half again the baseline's and the window it produced is slightly harder to make.
transferable_gaps.gap: Deeper edit walks fragment molecules instead of relocating them: the generator has no mechanism that keeps a useful molecular context intact while taking a longer structural step.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A multi-edit walk should be evaluated as a whole before it is proposed - rejecting or re-rolling a walk that destroys the molecular context it started from, rather than only stopping at the first failed operator call - and deletion-type edits should be bounded relative to the size of the molecule being edited. Genuine simplification must stay possible; what is missing is any test that a longer step still retains a usable molecule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the 13 matched post-divergence windows the Child covers 1006 distinct Murcko scaffolds against the baseline's 968 on the same 2339 proposals, and 858 of its 993 scaffolds never appear in the matched baseline session, so the proposal stream genuinely moved. Its class-level group census nevertheless stays within about three percentage points of the baseline on every group measured, and no new class appears anywhere. The clearest illustration is the one objective with a wide usable gradient: a basic sp3 nitrogen is present in 711 of 870 proposals and in all 50 of the highest-scoring molecules, but it is carried by a ring carbon sitting between both nitrogens - an aminal - in 94 percent of that top 50 and 253 of the larger proposals, while the standard saturated carriers of the same pharmacophore appear 3 times (piperazine), 25 times (piperidine) and 0 times (morpholine) in all 4350 molecules. Leading series also repeat within a class: on one objective six joint-best molecules share a score to four decimals and differ only in which halogen occupies two positions, and 67 of its 870 proposals collapse onto another when halogen identity is ignored.
transferable_gaps.gap: Extra structural reach relocates the scaffold without extending the functional-group vocabulary, so the generator cannot introduce a group class its population does not already carry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Breeding and mutation need a way to substitute a whole functional-group or ring-system unit for a chemically independent alternative that preserves the relationships the accepted feedback favoured, instead of only recombining and permuting the atoms and groups already present in the population. Added breadth in graph space does not supply added breadth in chemistry: the population is the vocabulary, so a wider or deeper search over the same operators re-arranges the same groups. Distinct canonical strings alone do not establish useful coverage, and no causal score benefit from broader coverage is established by this output evidence.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
